questions.question: What was the name of the Mahavir Swami Father's name? महावीर स्वामी के पिता का नाम क्या था?
questions.solution:
• Mahavir Swami was the son of Siddhartha, who was head of the Jantrika Clan of Vajji Sangh

Further Insight:

• Mahavir Jain

○ Also known as Mahavir Swami or Vardhamana or Kevalin or Jina or Arhant

○ Birth: 599 BC or 540 BC in Kundagram (Vashali), Bihar

○ Father: Siddhartha (Head of Jantrika clan of Vajji Sangh)

○ Mother: Trishala (sister of Lichhavi ruler Chetak)

○ Wife Yashoda (daughter of Kudinya gotra)

○ Daughter: Priyadarshana (Anojya)

○ Son-in-law: Jamali

○ Leaving home: At the age of 30 years on the orders of elder brother Nandivardhan.

○ Attainment of knowledge (Kaivalya) after 12 years of penance at the age of 42 years in Inhhä village under a sal tree on the banks of Rijupalika river

○ Nirvana (Death) 527 BC or 468 BC in Pavapuri (near present Rajgir

questions.question: Which river surrounded the Magadha Mahajanpada? मगध महाजनपद किस नदी से घिरा था?
questions.solution:
• Magadha Mahajanapada was surrounded by the rivers Ganga and son

Further Insight:

• Magadha

○ The name Magadha is first referenced in the Atharvaveda.

○ Situated between Anga and Vatsa, corresponding roughly to modern-day Patna and Gaya districts of Bihar and parts of eastern Bengal.

○ Boundaries:

■ North and West: Rivers Ganga and Son.

■ South: Vindhyan outcrop.

■ East: River Champa.

○ Early capital: Rajagriha (Girivraja), fortified by five hills.

○ Later capital: Pataliputra.

○ The earliest dynasty was established by Brihadratha.

○ Gained prominence under rulers like Bimbisara and Ajatsatru.

○ Neighboring States and Conflicts:

■ Licchavis of the Vajji confederacy were neighbors, separated by the Ganges River.

■ During Ajatsatru's reign, Magadha came into conflict with the Vajjis.

○ An ancient site at Pataliputra, where Ajatsatru's ministers constructed a fort to counter the Vajji confederacy.

○ The city of Giribbaja (Rajagriha) was encircled by five hills of historical importance:

■ Isigili

■ Vepulla

■ Yebhara

■ Pandava

■ Gijjhakuta
